preview: Ishaan Chandak shares his interview experience for a Summer Internship at Goldman Sachs in 2023, detailing the online assessment and two interview rounds.
content: Goldman Sachs Interview Experience Ishaan Chandak TY IT INTRODUCTION Hello, I'm Ishaan Chadnak, and I belong to the field of Information Technology. I would like to share my interview journey for the Summer Internship position at Goldman Sachs. ONLINE ASSESSMENT Date : 08/08/2023 Time: 8:00 AM (Duration →1 hour) Platform: HackerRank The online assessment consisted of 10 multiple-choice questions (MCQs), 2 coding questions, and 2 HR-related questions. We were allocated 50 minutes to complete the MCQs and coding questions, and an additional 10 minutes for the HR questions. For each correct MCQ answer, we earned +5 marks, while an incorrect answer resulted in a deduction of -2 marks. These are the questions I can recall from the assessment. MCQ’s: 1. We were presented with a mathematical expression and asked to determine the maximum stack size required when converting it from 'infix' to 'postfix' notation. 2. We were tasked with calculating the percentage reduction in the number of bits when applying "Huffman Coding" to encode a set of letters, along with their respective frequencies. 3. There was a coding problem involving multi-level inheritance and method overriding. We had to predict the output when invoking a member function from a derived class. 4. In a probability and combinatorics (PnC) question, we were asked to find the count of 5-digit numbers greater than or equal to 50,000 that contained the digits 6 and 9, with the condition that 9 must appear before 6, and all digits should be distinct. 5. We encountered a Resource Allocation Graph related to Operating Systems and CPU Scheduling, involving Request Edges and Resource Edges. The task was to determine the optimal process execution sequence to avoid deadlocks. 6. There was a question related to AVL Trees, although the exact details are not remembered. 7. We were given either the preorder or postorder traversal of a binary search tree and had to reconstruct the tree. 8. There was also a coding problem for which we needed to predict the output. Coding Questions: There were two questions in total. Out of which I was able to solve one because I had no time for the other one. First Question : A binary tree is given. We had to find the sum MagicSum of the tree. MagicSum is the sum of all Magic Nodes. Magic Node is the one whose one child is a factor of the other. In this we weren’t given the tree in the form of Nodes and its left or right child pointing to other nodes. In the question, The tree was represented as a series of relationships of each node to the Root node such as L, R, LL, LR.. and so on, where each node is left (L) to Root or left-left (LL) or right-left (RL) to Root and so on. Input Format: The first line of input contains an integer, N number of nodes in the tree The second line of input contains an Integer root which is the root of the tree.The next N-1 lines of input contain a string, S, and an integer, X separated by a single white space where X is a node in the tree and S is the relation between Root and X. Sample Input: 9 11 L 23 R 44 LL 13 LR 9 RL 22 RR 7 RLL 6 RLR 15 Second Question : An M x N matrix (P) is present. The terms alternate between ‘X’ and ‘Y’. There will be a list of queries. Each query is an array of size 3 ([a, b, c]). The first term represents the query type. The next two term represent the index of element in the matrix. The first query (a = 1) requires us to change the element at P[b][c] to ‘Y’. The second query (a = 2) requires us to change the element at P[b][c] to ‘X’. The third query (a = 3) requires us to print the matrix whose top left corner is P[b][c] and bottom right cornet is the end of the matrix (i.e, P[M-1][N-1]). HR Questions: There were total of two HR questions : What would your approach be when you are engaged in a project with a partner, and as the project's deadline approaches, your partner becomes unable to continue due to unforeseen circumstances? Can you recall a specific project where you invested significant effort, and what was your emotional response upon successfully completing it? ONLINE ASSESSMENT RESULTS On the 23rd of August, around 6:00 pm, the shortlist was announced. I was selected as one of the 12 students shortlisted for the interviews. INTERVIEW ROUND 1 Date : 25/08/2023 Time: 9:00 AM (Duration →1 hour) Platform: Zoom and HackerRank CodePair The interviewer asked me to give my introduction. Then she instructed me to open the Hackerrank codepair interface. The first question she asked was to concatenate two strings without changing the first two strings and print the answer, with the condition not to use the .concat() function. Then she moved to the second question: The Snakes and Ladders question, where I explained my thinking involving using a queue of pairs of pair<int, int>. After answering that, she asked, "If you have four different messages, how many minimum bits will you need to transmit that message?" I stated that Huffman coding can be used, and that it can be solved with just 2 bits if the message frequency is ignored. She questioned me about segmentation errors at the conclusion. INTERVIEW ROUND 2 Date : 25/08/2023 Time: 12:00 pm (Duration →40mins) Platform: Zoom The interviewer began by asking about my preferred programming language (C++). He then delved into Garbage Collectors typically associated with Java. Next, he inquired about Database Management Systems (DBMS), types of DBMS, key-value databases, document-based databases (MongoDB), and Columnar databases. The conversation shifted to multithreading, fundamentals of threads, distinctions between threads and processes, and how threads create the illusion of multiprocessing. Subsequently, he presented a scenario: a 100GB file with all white spaces replaced by "%" signs and asked for the most optimal approach to rectify this using a 4-core system. Finally, we discussed cloud computing, SaaS, Google's Compute Engine, and GPUs/TPUs. RESULTS I was one of the 3 students selected for internships.
